claim: The tracer particle material has a density of 1.03 g/cm3, which is independent of the diameter supplied.
validity_conditions: A bulk material property of the particle, so unlike almost everything else on this data sheet it does NOT depend on which diameter was bought and is usable before that gap closes. Three significant figures as printed; the sheet gives no tolerance and none is invented. Load-bearing twice over: it sets how fast a particle sediments against the diffusion being measured, and it is the rho in the number-density formula (tracer_number_density_from_diameter), whose agreement with the vendor's own table to 0.2 percent over five decades is the evidence that the table was computed from this value rather than measured. THE PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION IS WITHDRAWN -- THIS ENTRY IS NOT ABOUT THE BOTTLE ON THIS BENCH. On 2026-09-19 the person ruled that AFR-0500-COOH is not what is in use. Two facts force it: the bottle's label does not state a product identity (bottle_label_states_no_product, E3, and it was LOOKED AT -- so this is permanent doubt, not doubt pending a look), and the particles in use fluoresce under green excitation and show through a 605 band (particles_show_on_the_green_605_path, E2), which a particle emitting at 680 nm as this data sheet specifies does not do. The observation was made on this bench and the specification was not; 10.3 rule 1 binds a vendor exactly as it binds a prior project. WHAT IS AND IS NOT RETRACTED. This entry remains TRUE ABOUT THE ABVIGEN PRODUCT. Nothing in the data sheet has been found wrong about the thing the data sheet describes. What is withdrawn is that the thing it describes is ours. It is kept rather than deleted under rule 8, and because the next person to find this sheet needs to meet the record that it was examined and set aside. THE QUERY HANDLES WERE RENAMED, AND THAT IS THE ACTUAL REPAIR. The numbers used to answer to names beginning `tracer_`, and the word `tracer` is the claim that these are ours -- asserted in a string that nothing validates. Check 44 refused the `subject` fields on these entries and they were removed rather than gamed, which left the name as the only handle, so the claim did not disappear when the check rejected it: it moved somewhere no check reaches. The names now begin `abvigen_`, so a query for our tracer no longer lands here. The entry_id still begins `tracer_` and is deliberately left alone: it is the citation handle, it is referenced by name from the polystyrene dispersion entries, and renaming it would be a deletion under rule 8. A FOOTNOTE THAT IS REALLY THE WHOLE LESSON: renaming the number left this entry's `subject` dangling, and check 44 caught it immediately. The subject had been resolving only because a number in this same file carried the same name -- the entry was its own registry. That is the self-assertion manager-librarian named: a name that asserts its own subject is a subject nothing can refuse. The id is updated to match rather than removed, because consistency is the most that can be done inside this store; what would actually fix it is a registry for the sample, which does not exist and is raised.

identifiers.applies_to: the Abvigen catalogue product, NOT the bottle in use
